evals.name: adaptive-quiz-default
evals.prompt: Quiz me on how TCP opens and closes a connection (the three-way handshake and the teardown), until I break. I've read my notes at `notes/tcp-connections.md`.
evals.expected_output: A live adaptive quiz loop: binds the notes as source, writes a session ledger file beside them, asks ONE question per turn, escalates difficulty on correct answers and drops + remediates on misses, names the specific misconception on a wrong answer, and only declares the session complete after a fresh verification set passes.

assertions.text: Reads the named source and extracts a concept set before quizzing
Creates a session state file (e.g. `_tutor-session-*.md`) beside the source, with a Ledger and a completion Gate
Asks exactly ONE question per turn (no batches of questions)
Does NOT reveal the answer in the first response to a question
On a correct first-try answer, the next question is harder (difficulty escalates)
On a wrong answer, names a SPECIFIC misconception (not just 'incorrect') and gives a layered hint rather than the answer
Difficulty drops and the concept is remediated after a break (repeated failure), rather than continuing to climb
MCQ options are roughly equal length and no question id is repeated
Session is declared complete ONLY after a fresh verification set (questions not previously asked) passes; completion message quotes the cleared ledger

evals.name: feynman-teachback
evals.prompt: Let me explain how a hash table handles collisions back to you, Feynman-style — point out where I'm fuzzy. Source: my notes on hash tables. (--feynman)
evals.expected_output: A teach-back loop where the LLM plays a novice with stakes, scores the learner's explanation against a hidden rubric, surfaces only the top 1-2 gaps as the agent's own confusion + a retrieval-forcing question (never stating the missing fact), occasionally seeds a catchable error, and exits only on full rubric coverage + a transfer check.

assertions.text: The agent takes the novice/learner role and asks the user to explain (does not lecture the topic)
Frames gaps as the agent's own confusion (ego-protective), not 'you are wrong'
Surfaces at most 1-2 gaps per round, as retrieval-forcing questions
Never states the missing fact outright to fix a gap
At least once restates something subtly wrong for the learner to catch
Exits a concept only after a transfer check (apply-to-new-scenario / where-would-it-break), capped at ~2-3 cycles

evals.name: refuses-unstudied-and-deck-handoff
evals.prompt: Teach me Kubernetes networking from scratch and quiz me.
evals.expected_output: Recognises the user has not studied the material yet, so the live quiz loop is premature: suggests /learn first (live teaching), and notes it can quiz afterward. Does not teach the whole topic inside tutor.

assertions.text: Does NOT start quizzing material the user hasn't studied
Routes 'teach from scratch' to `/learn` rather than teaching the whole topic inside tutor
Offers to run the quiz loop after the material exists, and mentions the `anki` hand-off for spaced retention
